content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.5+ sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (especially -1.0+ sentiment) — model fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects in the opposite direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early downward turns, especially after sentiment shifts to negative.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overproject upward trend — ignore sentiment when it’s flat or weak.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs — if last 3-5 days show consolidation or decline, reduce forecast slope.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 5-10% to account for risk aversion.
- Model overestimates volatility in early forecast window — smooth out sharp peaks in first 7-10 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.
